I recall a particularly challenging project where I had to migrate a large-scale data pipeline to the cloud. Our team was handling over 500 million daily records, and we needed a containerized solution that could scale efficiently.

We were initially using AWS ECS (EC2 Container Service) with a fleet of EC2 instances, but as our workload grew, we faced issues with instance scaling and Fargate pricing. That's when I decided to explore AWS EKS (Elastic Container Service for Kubernetes).

I worked closely with our DevOps team to containerize our data workloads using Docker and deploy them on EKS. We used Terraform to provision our EKS cluster and configured AWS Load Balancer Controller to manage ingress traffic. With EKS, we were able to leverage Kubernetes' autoscaling capabilities, ensuring our cluster scaled up or down according to workload demands.

The result was impressive - we reduced our ETL runtime by 40% and saved 20% on costs. I also implemented a CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions, which automated our deployment process and reduced deployment cycles by 35%.

My experience with EKS and containerized data workloads has been invaluable. I've learned to appreciate the flexibility and scalability that EKS offers, especially when working with large-scale data pipelines.
